newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba plans monument to defiance of U.S. embargo.
newsitem.headline: Cuba plans monument to defiance of U.S. embargo.

text.p: Cuba plans to spend $150,000 raised by foreign solidarity groups on a monument in Havana symbolising defiance of the U.S. economic embargo against the communist-ruled island.
The first stone of the 65-foot (20-meter)-high monument, to be located near the U.S. Interests Section in Havana, will be laid during an international youth festival that Cuba is hosting in August.
The monument, designed by Brazilian architect Oscar Niemayer, will consist of a large concrete ring, broken by a 45-foot (14-meter) representation of the Cuban flag rising out of it.
Plans for its construction were announced in the Sunday Communist youth newspaper Juventud Rebelde, which said it was expected to be completed by next February.
Relations between Cuba and the United States have been hostile since the 1959 revolution that brought President Fidel Castro to power. The U.S. embargo was imposed in 1962.
